text.arabic_uthmani: سَيَقُولُونَ ثَلَٰثَةٌۭ رَّابِعُهُمْ كَلْبُهُمْ وَيَقُولُونَ خَمْسَةٌۭ سَادِسُهُمْ كَلْبُهُمْ رَجْمًۢا بِٱلْغَيْبِ ۖ وَيَقُولُونَ سَبْعَةٌۭ وَثَامِنُهُمْ كَلْبُهُمْ ۚ قُل رَّبِّىٓ أَعْلَمُ بِعِدَّتِهِم مَّا يَعْلَمُهُمْ إِلَّا قَلِيلٌۭ ۗ فَلَا تُمَارِ فِيهِمْ إِلَّا مِرَآءًۭ ظَٰهِرًۭا وَلَا تَسْتَفْتِ فِيهِم مِّنْهُمْ أَحَدًۭا

words.gloss_range: future-marked plural saying, anonymous and later judged as conjectural speech
words.root_gloss_range: saying, reporting, asserting, and in other forms fabricated attribution; locally a predicted human claim-cycle later downgraded by the unseen-guessing verdict

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the later unseen-guessing verdict that evaluates the preceding human speech
the later commanded saying that interrupts and redirects the repeated human speech-root

words.prose: {{ar:سَيَقُولُونَ}} ({{tr:sayaqūlūna}}) opens with a future-marked anonymous plural voice. Before the claimants are named or authorized, their speech is forecast as part of a repeated saying-chain that will be interrupted by {{ar:قُلْ}} ({{tr:qul}}). The later verdict {{ar:رَجْمًا بِٱلْغَيْبِ}} ({{tr:rajman bi-l-ghayb}}) narrows this speech from neutral reporting into exposed conjecture.

topics.headline: forecasted anonymous speech
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first claim is predicted and anonymous before the disputants can control the frame.
topics.reason: QAC supports the future-prefixed 3mp imperfect, and the rows converge on forecasted, unnamed claimants.

topics.headline: speech downgraded to conjecture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that ordinary saying is retrospectively heard as unsupported claim once the ayah names unseen-guessing.
topics.reason: The broad speech root can include neutral saying and fabricated attribution; locally the conjectural edge is licensed by the later phrase, not by the verb alone.

topics.headline: saying refrain before command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a repeated human speech-root that builds until the command redirects speech to the messenger.
topics.reason: The three report verbs and later imperative are concrete local repetitions, with an inter-ayah speech background from 18:21.

words.gloss_range: indefinite nominative cardinal opening the first compressed count claim
words.root_gloss_range: three, triad, and group-of-three value; locally the first conjectural number in an ascending series
words.prose: {{ar:ثَلَٰثَةٌ}} ({{tr:thalāthatun}}) gives a bare, indefinite count with the counted group left implicit. The number sounds like a complete assertion, but the following ordinal-and-dog phrase shows that the claim is still being assembled, and the wider sequence turns it into the first step of escalating odd-number conjecture.

topics.headline: compressed first count
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first number stands abruptly in the claim slot while the actual sleepers remain unstated.
topics.reason: QAC gives a nominative indefinite numeral, and the rows support ellipsis plus dependence on the following ordinal-dog phrase.

topics.headline: escalating form pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first count belongs to an ascending three-five-seven sequence, with recitational pressure at the numeral-ordinal boundary.
topics.reason: The sequence is local and the variant/contact rows are valid form evidence, but they show pressure around the claim-form rather than proving the count.

words.gloss_range: construct ordinal with suffix, making the dog their claimed fourth
words.root_gloss_range: fourthness, quartering, dwelling or encampment associations; locally an ordinal role bound to the group
words.prose: {{ar:رَّابِعُهُمْ}} ({{tr:rābiʿuhum}}) does not leave fourthness abstract. The construct and suffix bind the ordinal to the group, so the dog is cast as the one occupying a fourth-place role inside the claim. The wider root field can brush the cave-dwelling setting, but the local job is ordinal inclusion.

topics.headline: bound ordinal role
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the fourth is grammatically attached to them as a role in the counted set, not as a detached aside.
topics.reason: The active-participle ordinal in construct with the suffix supports a bound role within the number formula.

topics.headline: dwelling root color
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a faint dwelling-field resonance beside the cave setting, while the local sense remains ordinal fourthness.
topics.reason: The root range supports dwelling associations, but QAC and syntax select the ordinal noun here.

words.gloss_range: construct noun with suffix, the dog grammatically attached to the sleepers in the first count
words.root_gloss_range: dog, trained pursuit, clasping, guarding, and volatile animal force; locally the possessed dog as a stable participant in the claims
words.prose: {{ar:كَلْبُهُمْ}} ({{tr:kalbuhum}}) makes the dog theirs in grammar, not a loose animal beside the story. The dog becomes the invariant detail across competing numbers and recalls the visible threshold dog from 18:18, while the root field adds guarded attachment rather than making the dog a wild threat here.

topics.headline: possessed dog as constant
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the dog remains grammatically attached and structurally constant while the human numbers fluctuate.
topics.reason: Construct morphology and repeated in-ayah placement support the dog as the fixed element in the claim formulas.

topics.headline: guarded animal field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the dog carries companionship, guarding, and restraint pressure, while the local noun still simply names their dog.
topics.reason: The V4/root rows support animal, pursuit, clasping, and rabid branches; local construct grammar narrows these into controlled attachment and salience.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction that adds the second saying clause
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) joins the second finite saying clause directly to the first dog formula. The five-count is added as another coordinated human assertion, with no marker that it corrects the first claim.

topics.headline: coordinated second claim
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second count is placed beside the first as another claim in the chain, not as an authorized correction.
topics.reason: The particle coordinates the next finite verb and preserves the list-like report structure.

words.gloss_range: unprefixed anonymous plural saying in the repeated report chain
words.root_gloss_range: saying and asserting; locally an iterative report verb immediately exposed to the conjecture verdict

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the following accusative verdict that evaluates the manner of the middle saying clause

words.prose: {{ar:يَقُولُونَ}} ({{tr:yaqūlūna}}) repeats the anonymous plural speech without the future marker of the opening verb. It keeps the debate moving as a public refrain, and its clause is the one immediately followed by {{ar:رَجْمًا}} ({{tr:rajman}}), so the report verb becomes the doorway into an evaluative verdict on the manner of saying.

topics.headline: anonymous repeated report
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second report stays anonymous and formulaic, weakening its authority as sourced knowledge.
topics.reason: The 3mp imperfect has an implicit plural subject and lacks the opening future particle while repeating the speech formula.

topics.headline: gateway to conjecture verdict
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this saying clause is not left neutral; the following accusative verdict evaluates how the speech is performed.
topics.reason: The middle report governs the five-count and is followed by the accusative evaluative phrase.

words.gloss_range: second indefinite cardinal in the same number-plus-ordinal template
words.root_gloss_range: five, fifth, and organized fivefold grouping; locally the second polished but conjectural count
words.prose: {{ar:خَمْسَةٌ}} ({{tr:khamsatun}}) repeats the same polished count-template as the first claim. Its formal exactness, contact with the following ordinal, and even the root’s organized-five associations make the claim sound neat, but the ayah immediately frames it as conjecture rather than knowledge.

topics.headline: parallel polished count
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second number is formally neat and template-bound, which makes its lack of knowledge sharper.
topics.reason: The feminine cardinal and following masculine ordinal repeat the earlier syntactic template, with variant/contact evidence at the boundary.

topics.headline: exactness without knowledge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that exact numerical language can still be a surface of conjecture.
topics.reason: The broader five and military-organization field can color the precision, but the local context brands this exactness as unsupported.

words.gloss_range: construct ordinal with suffix, making the dog their claimed sixth
words.root_gloss_range: sixthness and one-sixth apportionment; locally an ordinal construct in the second formula

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the first ordinal-dog formula mirrored by the second ordinal

words.prose: {{ar:سَادِسُهُمْ}} ({{tr:sādisuhum}}) mirrors {{ar:رَّابِعُهُمْ}} ({{tr:rābiʿuhum}}) as a bound ordinal role: the dog is made their sixth inside the formula. The root’s fractional and apportioning feel gives the count an air of precision, but the surrounding verdict keeps that precision from becoming certainty.

topics.headline: second bound ordinal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the dog again occupies a grammatically attached ordinal role, mechanically patterned after the first claim.
topics.reason: The construct ordinal plus suffix and active-participle form parallel the first ordinal-dog formula.

topics.headline: precise apportionment color
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that technical apportionment overtones heighten the irony of a count the ayah does not validate.
topics.reason: The root and rarity evidence supports precision coloring, but the local function remains a simple ordinal in a conjectural formula.

words.gloss_range: second occurrence of the possessed dog inside the rejected count formula
words.root_gloss_range: dog and attachment field; locally the invariant dog-slot in the five-count

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the explicit conjecture label following the second dog-slot

words.prose: {{ar:كَلْبُهُمْ}} ({{tr:kalbuhum}}) stays in the same dog-slot while the number changes. Here the remembered dog is pulled into the very claim that will be labeled {{ar:رَجْمًا بِٱلْغَيْبِ}} ({{tr:rajman bi-l-ghayb}}), showing how even a true narrative detail can be misused inside unsafe enumeration.

topics.headline: dog slot in rejected count
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the dog remains stable even when the surrounding number is exposed as conjectural.
topics.reason: The rows converge on identical placement and the immediate proximity of the explicit conjecture verdict.

words.gloss_range: accusative verbal noun evaluating the speech as conjectural pelting
words.root_gloss_range: stoning, pelting, conjecturing, meteoric defense, and accursed expulsion; locally a metaphorical verdict on unsupported speech
words.prose: {{ar:رَجْمًا}} ({{tr:rajman}}) is the ayah’s hard evaluative blow against the counting dispute. Grammatically it can describe the manner of their saying or intensify the speech-act itself, and semantically it makes conjecture feel like pelting at what cannot be seen. The surah has already used the same root for threatened physical stoning in 18:20; here the violence shifts into speech.

topics.headline: accusative verdict on speech
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verse does not merely call the count wrong; it grammatically judges the way the speech is being performed.
topics.reason: The accusative verbal noun is locally attached to the saying sequence as manner or intensifying event-noun.

topics.headline: stoning metaphor for conjecture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices conjecture pictured as violent throwing into the unseen rather than harmless speculation.
topics.reason: The root field and the explicit 18:20 echo support the move from physical stoning to epistemic aggression.

topics.headline: harsh sound texture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the phrase’s abrasive sound supports the semantic force of the verdict.
topics.reason: The phonetic rows identify a local texture around the dismissal phrase; it supports, rather than replaces, the grammatical and semantic verdict.

words.gloss_range: preposition linking the pelting-verdict to the unseen domain

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the verbal noun carried by the preposition into the unseen domain
the governed unseen noun that receives the conjectural pelting image

words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) is the hinge that carries {{ar:رَجْمًا}} ({{tr:rajman}}) into {{ar:ٱلْغَيْبِ}} ({{tr:al-ghayb}}). The preposition lets the phrase be heard as pelting in, with, or at the unseen, so the speech-act is defined by its relation to inaccessible knowledge.

topics.headline: prepositional unseen hinge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a small preposition turns physical pelting language into an epistemic verdict about the unseen.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the following definite noun and supports locative, instrumental, or directional nuance without requiring one exclusive gloss.

words.gloss_range: definite unseen domain governed by the preposition in the conjecture verdict
words.root_gloss_range: absence, hiddenness, unseen knowledge, and speech about the absent; locally the bounded realm human guessing may not penetrate
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْغَيْبِ}} ({{tr:al-ghayb}}) names the unseen as a recognized domain, not just a vague mystery. The sleepers’ reality is absent from human view, so the counts become speech about what cannot be verified. The word also becomes a hinge: it labels the preceding guesses before the final count is heard, and it anticipates the later statement that unseen knowledge belongs to God in 18:26.

topics.headline: definite absent unseen domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the debate crosses into a recognized unseen realm where ordinary counting has no access.
topics.reason: The definite noun and root rows support both hiddenness and concrete absence as the local epistemic boundary.

topics.headline: knowledge and unseen pairing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the unseen is being transferred from human conjecture to divine knowledge, with 18:26 later making that ownership explicit.
topics.reason: The co-occurrence and echo rows tie this phrase to the knowledge roots in this ayah and to the later divine ownership of unseen knowledge in 18:26.

topics.headline: structural checkpoint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the unseen phrase interrupts the enumeration before the final claim, so that final claim is heard under an already stated warning.
topics.reason: The phrase closes the dismissal insertion between the second and third saying clauses.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction resuming the third saying after the dismissal phrase

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the inserted verdict after which the third saying clause resumes

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) resumes the saying-chain after {{ar:رَجْمًا بِٱلْغَيْبِ}} ({{tr:rajman bi-l-ghayb}}). The third count therefore enters as another coordinated human assertion, but it is now heard after the ayah has already named the arena as unseen conjecture.

topics.headline: restart after dismissal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the third claim is syntactically resumed after an inserted verdict, giving it a different listening environment.
topics.reason: The conjunction restarts a finite report clause after the accusative-prepositional dismissal phrase.

words.gloss_range: third anonymous plural saying before the command pivot
words.root_gloss_range: saying and asserting; locally the last human report before commanded correction

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the following imperative that interrupts the human saying chain

words.prose: {{ar:يَقُولُونَ}} ({{tr:yaqūlūna}}) keeps the final count grammatically on the side of human reported speech. It is still anonymous and unprefixed, yet it stands in the terminal position before {{ar:قُلْ}} ({{tr:qul}}), where the repeated human speech-root is reclaimed by commanded response.

topics.headline: anonymous final report
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that even the final, fuller count remains anonymous human assertion rather than revealed knowledge.
topics.reason: The third 3mp imperfect follows the dismissal phrase and lacks the opening future marker, preserving the report status.

topics.headline: terminal speech before command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final human saying is positioned for interruption by the divine command.
topics.reason: The final report begins the last count and is followed not by another human claim but by the imperative.

words.gloss_range: third cardinal number, structurally privileged but still redirected to divine knowledge
words.root_gloss_range: seven and completion/fullness, with a nearby wild-beast root edge; locally the final reported number before correction

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the dismissal phrase not immediately repeated after the seven-count

words.prose: {{ar:سَبْعَةٌ}} ({{tr:sabʿatun}}) is the final number in the ascending series. Its discourse environment is different: no immediate {{ar:رَجْمًا بِٱلْغَيْبِ}} ({{tr:rajman bi-l-ghayb}}) follows it, and the next movement is the command to say that the Lord knows best. That framing may privilege the count structurally, but the ayah still redirects certainty away from human enumeration.

topics.headline: structurally privileged seven
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the seven-count receives a different frame from the five-count while still yielding to divine knowledge.
topics.reason: The absence of immediate dismissal and following command are local structural facts; they privilege the claim's frame without turning it into an explicit divine confirmation.

topics.headline: wild-tame edge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a subtle wild-beast resonance beside the repeated dog, while the local word remains the cardinal seven.
topics.reason: The root field supports the animal edge, but the local grammatical sense is the numeral.

words.gloss_range: marked conjunction before the final ordinal-dog phrase

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the final ordinal introduced by this marked conjunction

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) before {{ar:ثَامِنُهُمْ}} ({{tr:thāminuhum}}) breaks the earlier template. The first two formulas move straight from number to ordinal; here the conjunction makes the dog’s eighth-place linkage syntactically marked and leaves the final claim suspended rather than simply identical to the earlier rejected patterns.

topics.headline: marked eighth link
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final ordinal is introduced differently, so the dog-slot no longer sounds like a plain repetition.
topics.reason: The conjunction is locally present only before the final ordinal, but its exact grammatical label remains debated.

topics.headline: eight-conjunction tradition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices why some grammatical tradition hears the conjunction as a special signal at the eighth item, while local analysis should not depend on that label alone.
topics.reason: The special-conjunction interpretation is a known grammatical claim with proposed parallels at 9:112 and 39:73, but local output should retain it as an interpretive pressure rather than a governing rule.

words.gloss_range: construct ordinal with suffix under the marked conjunction
words.root_gloss_range: eighthness and price or value fields; locally the dog as their eighth in the final formula
words.prose: {{ar:ثَامِنُهُمْ}} ({{tr:thāminuhum}}) binds eighthness to the group, but unlike the earlier ordinals it is introduced by the marked conjunction. The root also brushes price and value language, giving the final dog-inclusion a surplus of significance, though the local sense remains ordinal eighthness.

topics.headline: marked construct eighth
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the dog is bound to the group as their eighth in a syntactically distinguished final formula.
topics.reason: Construct morphology and the preceding conjunction distinguish this ordinal from the earlier fourth and sixth formulas.

topics.headline: value field color
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a value-field undertone around the eighth member, while the local grammar keeps the word as an ordinal.
topics.reason: The root can carry price/value associations and those are Quranically visible in places such as 2:41, 3:77, and 9:9, but here they color rather than replace eighthness.

words.gloss_range: final possessed dog occurrence after the marked eighth formula
words.root_gloss_range: dog, attachment, guarding, clasping; locally the invariant dog in the syntactically distinct final count
words.prose: {{ar:كَلْبُهُمْ}} ({{tr:kalbuhum}}) remains the refrain, but its final occurrence follows the only marked ordinal-link. It gathers the earlier in-ayah repetitions and the narrative dog from 18:18 into the last human claim, making the dog the stable detail around which the competing numbers turn.

topics.headline: dog after marked frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the dog is still constant, but the final syntax changes how that constant is attached to the count.
topics.reason: The third occurrence follows the exceptional conjunction-plus-ordinal frame rather than the earlier direct ordinal templates.

topics.headline: refrain and narrative recall
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the dog is the stable remembered element from the story amid variable human enumeration.
topics.reason: The rows tie the invariant refrain to the visible narrative dog of 18:18.

words.gloss_range: second-person masculine imperative redirecting speech from report to commanded response
words.root_gloss_range: saying and commanding speech; locally the authorized reply that interrupts anonymous plural claims

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the authorized content of the commanded reply

words.prose: {{ar:قُلْ}} ({{tr:qul}}) turns the repeated speech-root from anonymous plural assertion into a direct command to the messenger. It is the imperative of the saying root, not a scarcity root, and it makes {{ar:رَبِّي أَعْلَمُ}} ({{tr:rabbī aʿlamu}}) the authorized counter-statement after the human refrain.

topics.headline: imperative authority pivot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that authority shifts from what they say to what the messenger is commanded to say.
topics.reason: QAC and morphology support a 2ms imperative, and the local structure places it after three plural report verbs.

topics.headline: authoritative say-frame echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a broader surah pattern in which commanded speech refers disputed matters back to the Lord, with 18:29 offering another such frame.
topics.reason: The row's wording risks treating the local imperative as a scarcity-root form; QAC blocks that root claim, but the 18:29 commanded-speech comparison remains useful.

words.gloss_range: construct Lord-title with first-person suffix
words.root_gloss_range: lordship, nurturing, governing, increasing, and bringing to completion; locally the messenger’s Lord as source of the corrective knowledge
words.prose: {{ar:رَبِّي}} ({{tr:rabbī}}) makes the answer personal and authoritative: the messenger is ordered to refer the disputed number to my Lord. The title does more than name authority; its root field evokes the One who governs, nurtures, and brings the sleepers’ affair to completion, so their true count is not a detachable statistic.

topics.headline: personal Lord authority
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the correction moves from anonymous public debate to the messenger's confessed Lord.
topics.reason: The construct with first-person suffix licenses the personal invocation of divine authority.

topics.headline: nurturing completion field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the Lord who knows the number is also the One who has governed the sleepers' whole process.
topics.reason: The root field supports lordship, nurture, and completion; locally this enriches the divine title without displacing it.

words.gloss_range: elative predicate specifying superior divine knowledge over their number
words.root_gloss_range: knowing, signs, marks, and ordered knowledge; locally the Lord knows best the disputed count

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the prepositional phrase specifying the disputed count as the domain of divine knowledge
the later knowledge verb that contrasts restricted human knowing with divine knowledge

words.prose: {{ar:أَعْلَمُ}} ({{tr:aʿlamu}}) answers the numbers with knowledge, not with another number. The elative is completed by {{ar:بِعِدَّتِهِمْ}} ({{tr:bi-ʿiddatihim}}), so the correction targets the exact disputed count, while the following {{ar:يَعْلَمُهُمْ}} ({{tr:yaʿlamuhum}}) shows how divine knowledge contrasts with restricted human access.

topics.headline: targeted divine knowledge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the reply does not stay general; it locates knowledge precisely over the disputed number.
topics.reason: The elative predicate is syntactically completed by the following prepositional phrase naming the count.

topics.headline: knowledge over conjecture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah’s central contrast: divine knowing replaces pelting at the unseen.
topics.reason: The root contrast with the conjecture phrase and the unseen-knowledge pairing are local and explicit.

topics.headline: knowledge root echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the knowledge-root moving from divine superlative to the later restriction on human knowing.
topics.reason: The same root recurs in the next knowledge clause and supports the divine-to-human contrast.

topics.headline: sign and order color
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a sign-and-mark field around knowledge, while the local claim remains that the Lord knows best.
topics.reason: The root can include sign and landmark fields, but the local grammar selects knowing rather than a separate sign-reading topic.

words.gloss_range: preposition specifying the domain of divine knowing

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the elative whose domain this preposition specifies
the count noun governed through this preposition

words.prose: {{ar:بِ}} ({{tr:bi}}) focuses {{ar:أَعْلَمُ}} ({{tr:aʿlamu}}) onto {{ar:عِدَّتِهِمْ}} ({{tr:ʿiddatihim}}). It marks the exact domain of superior knowledge: not a vague assertion inserted into the debate, but divine knowledge of their count.

topics.headline: domain of knowing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the preposition pins the correction to the precise object of dispute.
topics.reason: The preposition extends or specifies the elative's scope toward the count noun.

words.gloss_range: construct count noun with suffix, gathering the disputed numbers into their true count
words.root_gloss_range: counting, numbering, preparation, and measured term; locally the sleepers' count known by God
words.prose: {{ar:عِدَّتِهِمْ}} ({{tr:ʿiddatihim}}) gathers the scattered numbers into one abstract count that belongs to them and is placed under divine knowledge. The root can also carry preparation and measured-term pressure, so the word quietly expands the issue beyond arithmetic, but locally it names the true count that human claims tried to seize.

topics.headline: true count under knowledge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the free-floating numbers are resolved into one count attached to the sleepers and governed by knowledge.
topics.reason: The construct suffix binds the count to the sleepers, and the clause places it under the Lord's knowing.

topics.headline: count and term range
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the root field can suggest ordered preparation or a measured term, while the local phrase selects their number.
topics.reason: The broader root range is valid, but the immediate object of knowledge is the disputed count.

words.gloss_range: negative particle opening a negation-exception restriction

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the exception particle that closes the negation frame opened here

words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) begins the restriction that will be closed by {{ar:إِلَّا}} ({{tr:illā}}). After the Lord’s superior knowledge is stated, the grammar sharply limits human knowing to a small exception.

topics.headline: negation-exception opening
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that human knowledge is not merely described as weak; it is formally restricted by a strong negation-exception frame.
topics.reason: The particle opens the formal exclusivity construction completed by the exception particle.

words.gloss_range: transitive knowing verb with the sleepers as object inside the restriction
words.root_gloss_range: knowing and recognizing; locally limited human knowledge of the sleepers themselves

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the delayed singular exception subject anticipated by the verb form

words.prose: {{ar:يَعْلَمُهُمْ}} ({{tr:yaʿlamuhum}}) repeats the knowledge root but now under negation. Its object suffix makes the sleepers themselves the object of restricted human knowledge, not only the number as an abstract datum, and the delayed {{ar:قَلِيلٌ}} ({{tr:qalīlun}}) keeps that access grammatically small.

topics.headline: restricted knowledge of them
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the restriction concerns knowing the sleepers themselves, not just owning a statistic about them.
topics.reason: The verb takes the plural object suffix and is bounded by the negation-exception frame.

topics.headline: grammar of smallness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the singular verb anticipating a singular exception, so scarcity is felt before it is named.
topics.reason: The singular masculine verb anticipates the delayed singular subject in the exception phrase.

words.gloss_range: exception particle closing the restriction on human knowledge

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the negation particle whose restriction is closed by this exception particle

words.prose: {{ar:إِلَّا}} ({{tr:illā}}) closes the restriction opened by {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}). It does not create broad confidence; it leaves only a small exception against the background of general ignorance.

topics.headline: exception closing restriction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the grammar permits only an exception, not an open field of human expertise.
topics.reason: The particle licenses the following exception noun within the negation frame.

words.gloss_range: nominative singular indefinite exception to the knowledge restriction
words.root_gloss_range: fewness, smallness, scarcity, and reduction; locally the small unspecific group who know

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the earlier command that forms a sound echo with the fewness term

words.prose: {{ar:قَلِيلٌ}} ({{tr:qalīlun}}) is the only human-side exception left by the grammar, and it remains indefinite. The word keeps the exception scarce and unspecified, resisting broad confidence. Its sound also lightly answers {{ar:قُلْ}} ({{tr:qul}}): the commanded response belongs beside fewness, not noisy multiplication of claims.

topics.headline: scarce unspecified knowers
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the exception is intentionally small and unspecified, so the disputants cannot claim broad authority.
topics.reason: The nominative singular indefinite after the exception particle supports a scarce, open-ended exception.

topics.headline: command and fewness sound echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a tight sound link between the command to speak and the few who know.
topics.reason: The rows identify a local consonantal echo that supports the speech-versus-fewness contrast.

words.gloss_range: consequential conjunction leading from knowledge limitation to prohibition

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the consequence-prohibition phrase launched by this conjunction

words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) makes the prohibition follow from the knowledge correction. Because the Lord knows best and human knowledge is restricted, the next move is not more counting but disciplined restraint: {{ar:فَلَا تُمَارِ}} ({{tr:fa-lā tumāri}}).

topics.headline: knowledge-to-prohibition consequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that doctrine immediately becomes speech discipline.
topics.reason: The conjunction attaches the prohibition to the prior knowledge statement as a consequence or explicative follow-on.

words.gloss_range: prohibitive particle governing the jussive dispute verb

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the jussive dispute verb governed by this prohibitive particle

words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) turns the knowledge boundary into a direct prohibition. It governs {{ar:تُمَارِ}} ({{tr:tumāri}}) in the jussive, so the response to uncertain knowledge is not intensified debate but command-level restraint.

topics.headline: direct prohibitive restraint
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah moves from epistemic correction to an authoritative ban on disputing.
topics.reason: The particle is prohibitive and governs the following jussive verb.

words.gloss_range: jussive Form III dispute verb under prohibition, with surface evidence noting root-analysis confusion
words.root_gloss_range: disputing, reciprocal contention, doubt, and agitated back-and-forth; locally prohibited disputation with only a narrow outward allowance

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the exception phrase that restricts the prohibited dispute to outward engagement

words.prose: {{ar:تُمَارِ}} ({{tr:tumāri}}) names reciprocal disputation under prohibition, not private uncertainty. The clipped jussive form fits the command’s restraint, and the following {{ar:إِلَّا مِرَاءً ظَاهِرًا}} ({{tr:illā mirāʾan ẓāhiran}}) keeps any engagement outward and limited. The surface data’s swaying-root note can color the instability of argument, but the local dispute field is secured by the cognate noun that follows.

topics.headline: prohibited dispute with narrow allowance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that disputation is not simply erased; it is restricted to one outward, controlled form.
topics.reason: The prohibitive particle governs the verb, and the later exception phrase supplies the narrow allowance.

topics.headline: clipped jussive form
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the form itself grammatically shortened under prohibition, matching the curtailed argument.
topics.reason: The jussive analysis supports apocopation under the prohibitive particle.

topics.headline: reciprocal agitated contention
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the banned act is interactive, unstable contention rather than sincere inquiry.
topics.reason: Form III supports reciprocal disputation; the surface swaying-root evidence is treated as coloring because classical/local analysis points to the dispute root.

words.gloss_range: prepositional phrase scoping the dispute to the sleepers
words.prose: {{ar:فِيهِمْ}} ({{tr:fīhim}}) scopes the prohibition. The command does not ban all discussion; it restricts disputation about the sleepers, the very group whose number and identity have been made inaccessible to broad human knowledge.

topics.headline: dispute topic scope
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ban is targeted to arguing about the sleepers, not to speech in general.
topics.reason: The prepositional phrase functions topically and attaches the prohibited dispute to its subject matter.

words.gloss_range: exception particle introducing the sole permitted form of dispute

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the outward dispute phrase introduced as the sole exception

words.prose: {{ar:إِلَّا}} ({{tr:illā}}) opens the narrow exception inside the prohibition. What remains is not open argument, but only {{ar:مِرَاءً ظَاهِرًا}} ({{tr:mirāʾan ẓāhiran}}): an outward, bounded form of engagement.

topics.headline: limited exception to ban
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah restricts rather than simply forbids every possible response.
topics.reason: The exception particle introduces the sole permitted form after the prohibitive construction.

words.gloss_range: accusative verbal noun naming the permitted minimum of disputation
words.root_gloss_range: dispute, doubt, and drawing-out or extraction; locally the cognate dispute noun qualified by outwardness

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the cognate dispute verb echoed by this verbal noun

words.prose: {{ar:مِرَاءً}} ({{tr:mirāʾan}}) turns the prohibited verb into a named, bounded noun so the verse can define the only allowed type. The cognate echo with {{ar:تُمَارِ}} ({{tr:tumāri}}) makes the limit self-contained, while the root’s drawing-out image shows why the next word must keep the dispute at the surface.

topics.headline: cognate limited dispute
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the act of disputing is named as a controlled dose, not left as open contention.
topics.reason: The accusative verbal noun follows the cognate verb and is then qualified by the outward adjective.

topics.headline: drawing-out image
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices argument as a pulling-out or prolonging act, which makes the outward limit more forceful.
topics.reason: The concrete extraction branch is root-level imagery; local grammar selects dispute but can retain the image as pressure.

words.gloss_range: accusative active participle modifying the permitted dispute as outward
words.root_gloss_range: visible, outward, exterior, back, support, dominance, and alliance; locally outward surface-level argument

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the unseen domain contrasted by the outward-surface limit

words.prose: {{ar:ظَاهِرًا}} ({{tr:ẓāhiran}}) sets the permitted dispute at the visible surface. It answers {{ar:ٱلْغَيْبِ}} ({{tr:al-ghayb}}): argument may stay with what is outward and transparent, but it must not pretend to penetrate hidden reality. The support and dominance branches add a warning that even permitted argument must not become alliance-building polemic.

topics.headline: visible surface boundary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the allowed dispute is bounded by outward visibility, the opposite of hidden-knowledge claims.
topics.reason: The active participle agrees with the dispute noun and contrasts locally with the unseen phrase.

topics.headline: no dominating polemic
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that outward dispute is not allowed to harden into dominance, backing, or factional force.
topics.reason: The root can carry support and dominance fields; local syntax keeps the primary sense outward but allows the warning as secondary pressure.

words.gloss_range: conjunction coordinating the second prohibition with the first
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) links a second prohibition to the first. The ayah moves from not disputing about the sleepers to not seeking outside rulings about them, making consultation a separate practical danger rather than a mere restatement.

topics.headline: parallel second prohibition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that arguing and outsourcing authority are paired as two distinct violations after the knowledge boundary.
topics.reason: The conjunction coordinates a second prohibitive construction with its own jussive verb.

words.gloss_range: second prohibitive particle governing the consultation verb
words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) extends the boundary from public disputation to solicitation of rulings. The second prohibition prevents the uncertain voices from becoming consulted authorities.

topics.headline: second prohibitive extension
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah blocks not only argument but also appeal to suspect expertise.
topics.reason: The particle governs the following jussive consultation verb.

words.gloss_range: jussive Form X verb forbidding seeking a ruling or authoritative answer
words.root_gloss_range: seeking a ruling, authoritative answer, youth-field resonance, and opening a question; locally prohibited outsourcing of authority

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the full consultation frame: about them, from among them, no one

words.prose: {{ar:تَسْتَفْتِ}} ({{tr:tastafti}}) forbids seeking an authoritative answer from others about the sleepers. Form X makes the act a request for a ruling, while {{ar:فِيهِم مِّنْهُمْ أَحَدًا}} ({{tr:fīhim minhum aḥadan}}) fills out the whole frame: about them, from among them, no one. The same root field also recalls the youths of 18:13, so the word warns against seeking a verdict about the very youths whose story revelation has bounded.

topics.headline: no outsourced authority
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the prohibition targets outsourcing authority, not casual asking alone.
topics.reason: Form X and the surrounding prepositional/object frame support seeking a ruling or answer from another source.

topics.headline: clipped consultation jussive
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second prohibited verb is formally curtailed like the first.
topics.reason: The jussive form under prohibition supports the clipped ending and parallel with the dispute verb.

topics.headline: youth and ruling root echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the root field linking the sleepers as youths in 18:13 with the forbidden act of seeking a ruling about them in 18:22.
topics.reason: The inter-ayah echo is concrete and valuable, but it should color the prohibition rather than imply that youth is the selected local sense.

words.gloss_range: repeated topical prepositional phrase anchoring consultation to the sleepers
words.prose: {{ar:فِيهِمْ}} ({{tr:fīhim}}) repeats the same topical anchor from the dispute prohibition. Both banned actions, arguing and seeking rulings, are about the sleepers, so the contested group remains the shared object of restraint.

topics.headline: repeated topic anchor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that both prohibitions are tied to the same contested sleepers.
topics.reason: The repeated prepositional phrase links the dispute and consultation prohibitions around the same pronoun referent.

words.gloss_range: source or partitive prepositional phrase identifying whom not to consult
words.prose: {{ar:مِنْهُمْ}} ({{tr:minhum}}) marks the suspect source of consultation. The prohibition is circular in force: do not ask anyone from among the very people whose speech has been exposed as conjectural about the sleepers.

topics.headline: partitive source warning
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the answer must not be drawn from the same disputed human source pool.
topics.reason: The preposition can mark source or partitive origin, and the pronoun locally points to the disputing group rather than the sleepers.

topics.headline: circular prohibition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the logic of not asking the conjecturers to certify the matter they are conjecturing about.
topics.reason: The phrase sits between the topic phrase and the universal object, creating a warning against sourcing the answer from the exposed guessers.

words.gloss_range: indefinite accusative object under prohibition, giving universal negative scope
words.root_gloss_range: one, anyone, singularity, uniqueness, and exclusion; locally any individual whatsoever from them
words.prose: {{ar:أَحَدًا}} ({{tr:aḥadan}}) closes the ayah with total exclusion. Under the prohibition it means not a single consultant from among them, so the multiplied opinions end in one hard boundary. The broader singularity field can echo divine uniqueness in 112:1, but locally the force is universal negative: no one.

topics.headline: universal negative closure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the consultation ban closes on every possible individual, not only major authorities.
topics.reason: The indefinite noun under negation supplies universal negative scope and occupies the final word position.

topics.headline: singularity and exclusion field
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the root’s one-ness field compresses many claimants into a ban on any single person.
topics.reason: The root supports singularity and exclusion, with 112:1 as a theological contrast, but the local grammar selects generic any-one scope.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Words 1-14 stage three future-speech count formulas; words 15-33 answer with divine knowledge and limits on dispute and consultation.
baseline_models.mechanism: Repeated saying circulates rival counts. The first two are explicitly marked as conjectural projection into what is hidden, while the third remains grammatically distinct but is not authorized as known. Knowledge and exhaustive enumeration are relocated to the Lord, and the addressee is restricted to outward dispute without soliciting another verdict.

activation_trace.role: Circulating speech supplies the repeated public-claim frame rather than certified knowledge.
Saying by conjecture about the unseen explicitly classifies the first pair of count claims.
Concealment from eyes defines the inaccessible object toward which the guesses are cast.
Disclosure to a knower contrasts actual knowledge with the preceding circulation of claims.
Exhaustive enumeration names the precise object whose mastery is withheld from the speakers.
Sharp verbal contention supplies the regulated social action that follows unresolved counting.
What is exposed or apparent bounds the permitted dispute on the hidden matter.
Seeking a clarifying verdict is the consultation channel that the final prohibition closes.
Indefinite one under negation makes the ban on human consultation exhaustive.

changed_reading.before: The ayah lists competing headcounts and then vaguely advises against argument.
changed_reading.after: The ayah ranks speech acts: report the claims, mark conjecture, return exact enumeration to divine knowledge, and restrict both debate and consultation without forcing a final human count.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Across words 2-14, the proposed human counts rise from three to five to seven while the dog recurs at words 4, 8, and 14 as the next ordinal member.
baseline_models.mechanism: Every proposal preserves the relation of a named count followed by the dog as its ordinal successor. The varying numbers move, but the canine companion and its after-position do not, making inclusion and category boundary part of the counting problem.

activation_trace.role: The number three opens the first variable count.
The fourth position attaches the dog as successor to the first count.
The number five advances the variable count.
The sixth position again places the dog immediately after the proposed human count.
The number seven supplies the third and largest proposed count.
The eighth position repeats the same successor relation after seven.
The literal dog is the invariant companion across all three shifting formulas.

changed_reading.before: The dog is an incidental narrative detail repeated in each reported count.
changed_reading.after: The dog is the formula's stable term: each group counts the same companion after a changing human total, exposing uncertainty about membership and the boundary of the counted group.

context_deltas.mechanism: The context separates mere verbal output from warranted narration. At 18:5 a grave word exits mouths as falsehood; at 18:13 the account is traced as sequential narration in truth; at 18:15 a claim requires manifest authority and fabrication is named. The count sayings in 18:22 are therefore ranked by source and warrant, not merely by numerical content.

activation_trace.role: Intelligible speech supplies the verbal object whose existence does not itself establish truth.
Bringing something out of concealment makes mouth-output a visible event distinct from disclosure of fact.
Opening the mouth in speech localizes the unsupported claim at its bodily outlet.
Contradiction of truth classifies that mouth-output despite its emphatic wording.
Sequentially carried narration supplies the alternative mode of an accountable report.
Stable correspondence with reality explicitly warrants the narrated account.
Compelling proof supplies the evidentiary demand absent from bare assertion.
Manifest clarification defines what evidence would have to make publicly knowable.
Fabricated falsehood names the danger of manufacturing an account without authority.

structural_cues: 18:5 places lack of knowledge before mouth-output and falsehood; 18:13 changes to true sequential narration; 18:15 asks for manifest authority.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a mouth/falsehood sequence, true narration, and an evidentiary demand; I infer that source and warrant rank the 18:22 claims. A live alternative is that 18:5 and 18:15 regulate only their immediate theological claims, not every later count.

changed_reading.before: The three count propositions differ mainly in which number they assert.
changed_reading.after: Their decisive difference from knowledge is procedural: repeated and emphatic speech remains mouth-output until a truthful source or manifest authority warrants it.

context_deltas.mechanism: At 18:19 the youths question one another, circulate duration estimates, and then stop at their Lord's superior knowledge. This formally rehearses the claim-to-divine-knowledge turn of 18:22 inside the group before outsiders repeat it over their number.

activation_trace.role: Mutual questioning initiates uncertainty within the group itself.
Saying that operates as supposition supplies the same repeated estimate register heard in 18:22.
Remaining in a place supplies the uncertain duration being estimated.
A bounded duration provides the first rough estimate.
A part of the duration reduces the estimate without resolving it.
Lordship relocates final authority beyond the mutually questioning speakers.
Actual disclosure to the knower closes the estimate sequence without selecting a human answer.

structural_cues: 18:19 repeats saying around a whole-or-part duration estimate and ends with 'your Lord knows best'; 18:22 repeats the same turn for headcount.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the formal repetition; I read 18:19 as an internal rehearsal for the later public count dispute. The alternative is a looser parallel between two unrelated unknowns, duration and number.

changed_reading.before: The epistemic restraint of 18:22 is an abstract correction addressed only to later disputants.
changed_reading.after: The correction reuses the youths' own disciplined response to uncertainty: estimate may occur, but the sequence should terminate in acknowledged divine knowledge rather than factional certainty.

context_deltas.mechanism: The dog is not only the invariant successor in the count formulas. At 18:18 it is bodily extended at the cave's connected forecourt or door. Its stable grammatical after-position in 18:22 is sharpened by its spatial threshold position in the scene.

activation_trace.role: The literal dog remains the repeated successor after every changing count.
The fourth position begins the repeated grammatical placement just beyond the human count.
The sixth position preserves that successor placement in the second formula.
The eighth position preserves it in the third formula.
The same literal dog supplies the scene-level anchor for the counting invariant.
Extension against contraction gives the dog's threshold posture spatial reach.
The extended forelimbs materialize the posture at the boundary.
The forecourt or door connected to the dwelling locates the dog between interior group and exterior approach.

structural_cues: All three formulas put the dog after a proposed human count.
18:18 puts the dog at the cave's physical entrance with forelimbs extended.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies grammatical successor position and spatial threshold position; I infer that the latter sharpens the former into a category-boundary role. The alternative is simple narrative repetition with no designed relation between syntax and location.

changed_reading.before: The dog is merely added to each proposed total.
changed_reading.after: The dog marks the group's edge twice, physically at the cave threshold and grammatically at the count threshold, so disagreement concerns not only quantity but who or what is counted as inside.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately following speech rule conditions assertion about a future act, provides recovery after forgetting, and directs the speaker toward better guidance. This turns 18:22 from an isolated ban on argument into one instance of locally sustained speech discipline under limited knowledge.

activation_trace.role: Uttered assertion supplies the speech act placed under a prohibition and condition.
A knowable and reportable thing defines the broad object of the future claim.
Bringing an act about supplies the projected event the speaker cannot guarantee alone.
The following day places the assertion beyond present access.
Recovery of something after lapse supplies a correction path for the limited speaker.
Loss from memory names the human limitation that makes correction necessary.
Right judgment redirects speech toward a better course rather than defensive certainty.

structural_cues: 18:23-24 directly follows the count dispute with another 'do not say' construction, an exception, remembrance after forgetting, and a renewed 'say'.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adjacency and repeated speech commands; I infer a shared protocol for claims under temporal or epistemic limits. The alternative is that 18:23-24 concerns only promises about future action and does not generalize back to reported counts.

changed_reading.before: The closing commands in 18:22 only suppress an unproductive historical controversy.
changed_reading.after: They model revisable speech: acknowledge the limit, attach the claim to divine authority, permit correction, and seek guidance rather than compensating for uncertainty with stronger assertion.

context_deltas.mechanism: A precise duration formula follows the refused headcount, and the next ayah repeats 'say', superior divine knowledge, and the unseen before locating judgment with God. The sequence is not anti-number; it distinguishes a disclosed measure from an unauthorized enumeration of hidden persons.

activation_trace.role: Remaining in the cave supplies the duration that is openly numbered.
Three participates in an explicit disclosed magnitude rather than a reported rival claim.
Reaching the hundred scale fixes the main duration quantity.
The year branch supplies the unit of the disclosed count.
Increase appends a further quantity without opening rival estimates.
Nine supplies the explicit added amount.
Commanded utterance marks the authorized response formula.
Superior disclosure to the knower assigns authority over their duration.
The same stay remains an object of divine knowledge even after its number is stated.
What is hidden from eyes generalizes the knowledge boundary beyond the headcount.
Judgment between claimants locates final adjudication with the same authority that knows the hidden.

structural_cues: 18:25 states one number directly rather than reporting speakers; 18:26 repeats the focus ayah's 'say + God knows best + unseen' pattern.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the contrast between reported headcounts and a directly stated duration plus the repeated knowledge formula; I infer source-sensitive numeracy rather than distrust of counting itself. The alternative is that duration and headcount are separate topics with no general policy linking them.

changed_reading.before: The ayah discourages numerical inquiry because numbers about the story are spiritually irrelevant.
changed_reading.after: The ayah permits exact number when disclosed but refuses to manufacture number from hearsay; the issue is authorization and access, not numeracy.

context_deltas.mechanism: At 18:21 disclosure of the hidden youths immediately becomes public contention, rival construction speech, and a project asserted by the prevailing party. The count debate in 18:22 is thus a social afterlife of discovery, and the ban on seeking a verdict from any of them blocks factional possession of the revealed story.

activation_trace.role: Discovery of what was hidden initiates public handling of the youths.
Mutual pulling between parties turns discovery into a contested object.
Negotiating speech supplies the rival public proposals that precede the count sayings.
Joining material into a structure gives one faction a durable way to frame the discovered group.
Prevailing force explains why one proposal can dominate without becoming epistemically truer.
A place of prostration is the institutional form selected by the prevailing party.
Seeking a verdict names the channel through which a faction could be granted interpretive authority.
Exhaustive negation closes that channel to every factional claimant.

structural_cues: 18:21 orders discovery, dispute, rival building proposals, and the prevailing party's decision immediately before the count controversy.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the sequence from exposure to public competition; I infer that 18:22 resists social capture of the story by whichever party prevails. The alternative is that the building dispute and number dispute are adjacent but independent controversies.

changed_reading.before: The prohibition on consultation only prevents importing another weak historical opinion.
changed_reading.after: It also denies victorious or institution-building factions the right to convert social dominance into authority over the hidden persons they have publicly claimed.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because a perceptual scene is used to sharpen a discourse limit. It remains anchored in the focus contrast between hidden and apparent and in 18:18's explicit false reckoning from visible posture. Render it as an exploratory evidentiary boundary, not as a claim that 'apparent' lexically means 'visual evidence only'.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus ayah opposes casting speech into the hidden at word 10 to dispute kept apparent or exposed at word 28.

activation_trace.role: Concealment from eyes marks the domain unavailable to ordinary inspection.
Exposure and appearance bound the permitted mode of dispute.
Reckoning as supposition shows an observer deriving a wrong state from appearance.
Wakefulness supplies the visible but mistaken classification.
Sleep supplies the concealed actual state that contradicts the observer's reckoning.
Inspection and exposure trigger a powerful reaction without yielding full understanding.

changed_reading.before: An 'apparent dispute' is simply a brief or ordinary argument.
changed_reading.after: It may be a dispute deliberately kept at the exposed surface: appearance can be discussed, but the scene itself warns that visible posture does not disclose hidden reality.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it materializes the idiom of conjecture and links it to the prior construction dispute. It remains valid as an activation because the cited ر ج م branches supply stony harmful speech and accumulation while 18:21 supplies literal building over the hidden group. Render it explicitly as a material analogy, not as the required lexical sense of the phrase.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: Word 9 casts the disputed counts as رَجْمًا immediately before the hidden domain at word 10.

activation_trace.role: Harmful speech likened to stone-throwing turns unsupported count claims into verbal projectiles.
Accumulation of one thing upon another lets repeated claims harden into a layered public account.
The concealed persons are the inaccessible object onto which the verbal material is cast.
Factional pulling supplies the social force that turns memory into competing constructions.
Literal joining into a building provides the material analogue for fixing a claim over the hidden group.
The proposed place of prostration shows one public framing becoming durable institution.

changed_reading.before: The count guesses are harmless verbal noise after the building dispute.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, they are verbal monument-making: factions throw and stack claims over hidden persons, while the ayah prevents that accumulated speech from becoming authoritative knowledge.

strongest_changes: 18:19 internally rehearses the same estimate-to-'your Lord knows best' movement that 18:22 applies to public headcount.
18:25-26 distinguishes an explicitly disclosed duration number from hearsay enumeration, making the policy source-sensitive rather than anti-numerical.
The dog's repeated ordinal after-position is sharpened by its physical threshold position at 18:18.
The 18:21 sequence from discovery to factional building makes refusal of consultation a barrier against converting social dominance into authority.
summary.what_was_special: The ayah's restraint is operational rather than skeptical: it separates speech, warrant, number, appearance, and social authority while preserving multiple live readings of the invariant dog and the public handling of hidden persons.
remaining_uncertainties: The third count is syntactically distinguished from the two guesses explicitly labeled رَجْمًا بِٱلْغَيْبِ, but the packet does not authorize declaring it correct.
The relation between the dog's grammatical successor position and its spatial threshold position is inferential rather than lexical.
The surface-evidence and verbal-monument readings are branch-backed analogies and should not displace the stronger epistemic model.
The exact force of مِرَآءً ظَٰهِرًا may range from outward or evidence-bounded dispute to a merely limited, non-deep argument.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Repeated utterance does not accumulate into knowledge.** `ق و ل` B001 (“uttered speech”) repeats across three counts, while `ع ل م` B001 is reserved for the Lord and a few. The later warning against asserting tomorrow (18:23–24) extends the same limit from hidden past to hidden future. I infer that repetition gives speculation social mass but no epistemic gain. The ayah makes disciplined non-escalation the proper response.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 18:23–24 extended the discipline from hidden past counts to categorical claims over the hidden future.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Numbers hurled rather than counted.** `ر ج م/B004` explicitly supplies conjectural speech about the unseen, and `ر ج م/B002` supplies verbal pelting. The earlier threat `يَرْجُمُوكُمْ` (18:20) gives the material analogue, while this ayah repeats numerical claims without an evidentiary operation and contrasts them with divine knowledge of `عِدَّتِهِم`. I infer that unsupported enumeration behaves like stones thrown into darkness. The disputed counts read as aggressive projection, not as incomplete arithmetic.

2. **Dispute that extracts no valid yield.** `م ر ي/B003` is contentious disputing, while `م ر ي/B001` is drawing something out by rubbing or urging. The repeated claims and command to keep the dispute merely outward supply the friction; no new knowledge emerges from it. I infer that this argumentative “milking” lacks a source capable of yielding certainty. `فَلَا تُمَارِ` reads as a limit on an epistemically unproductive extraction process.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 18:23–24 extended the warning from guessed past counts to confident future claims, confirming that the issue is speech outrunning knowledge.

baseline.text: Bazıları, Onlar üç kişiydi, dördüncüleri köpekleriydi, diyecek. Bazıları bilinmeyen hakkında tahmin yürüterek, Beş kişiydi, altıncıları köpekleriydi, diyecek. Bazıları da, Yedi kişiydi, sekizincileri köpekleriydi, diyecek. De ki: Rabbim onların sayısını daha iyi bilir; onları ancak az kişi bilir. Bu yüzden onlar hakkında yalnızca açık olan ölçüde tartış ve bunlar hakkında o kişilerden hiçbirine soru sorma.

findings.text: Üç ayrı sayımın tekrar tekrar söylenmesi bilgi biriktirmez; söz toplumsal ağırlık kazanırken bilgi Allah'a ve pek az kişiye ait kalır.
Sayı tahminleri, hesaplanmış sonuçlardan çok bilinmeyene atılmış taşlar gibi sunulur.
Bu konuda uzatılan çekişme gerçeği sağan bir araştırma değil, geçerli bir sonuç üretmeyen kısır bir sıkıştırmadır.

error_profile.preserves: Uc kokenli bir adla uzak iliskiyi koruyabilir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Sayi olarak uc ve sayisal bicimlerdir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Bir butunun uc parcadan biri veya uce bolunmesiyle ilgilidir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Iki dal da uc sayisina dayanir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal ucun sayi degerini verir; komsu dal ise bir butunun uc parcaya oranlanmis payini veya bolunmesini anlatir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Sayi adinin kendisini ve dagilimli sayimi kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Bir kisinin veya seyin ucuncu olmasini ya da ikiye eklenerek ucu tamamlamasini kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Iki dalda da uc sayisi belirleyicidir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal nicel sayiyi adlandirir; komsu dal sira, uyelik veya tamamlama iliskisini adlandirir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Genel sayi ve sayisal bicimlerdir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Haftanin belli bir gununun adidir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Gun adi tarihsel olarak sayi bicimiyle iliskili gorunur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Okur icin karisabilecek nokta bicimsel yakinliktir; anlamda biri sayi, oburu takvim adidir.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Adaylar sayi, pay, sira, gun ve kok icindeki ozel kullanimlar etrafinda denetlendi; en yararli ayrimlar yakin ic dallardadir.
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه عدد الثلاثة وما تصرف منه في التذكير والتأنيث والعشرات والمئات والألوف وصيغ التوزيع مثل ثلاث ومثلث
branches.source_phrase_ar: اثنان وثلاثة (maqayis)؛ الثلاثة في عدد المذكر والثلاث في عدد المؤنث (sihah)؛ الثلاثة من العدد (tahdhib)؛ الثلاثة والثلاثون والثلاث والثلاثمائة وثلاثة آلاف (mufradat)

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه الثلث والثلثان والأثلاث وتقسيم الشيء أثلاثا وأخذ ثلث المال وما بلغ ثلثيه
يدخل فيه كونه ثالثا أو أحد الثلاثة أو إتمام الاثنين ثلاثة أو مجيء الفرس ثالثا في السباق
يدخل فيه الحبل المفتول على ثلاث قوى والمزادة من ثلاثة جلود والكساء من ثلاثة أشياء والشيء ذو الأركان الثلاثة وما كان على ثلاثة أثناء أو ثلاثة أذرع
يدخل فيه الناقة التي تملأ ثلاثة آنية عند الحلب أو تحلب من ثلاثة أخلاف أو يبس ثلاثة من أخلافها أو صر منها ثلاثة أخلاف
يدخل فيه اسم اليوم الثلاثاء وتثنيته وجمعه
يدخل فيه الحيد النادر من الجبل الذي يضم إلى صخرتين لتنصب عليه القدر ويدخل فيه رمي القوم بثالثة الأثافي في الأمر العظيم
يدخل فيه الشراب الذي طبخ حتى ذهب ثلثاه وبقي ثلثه
يدخل فيه الرجل الذي يمحل بأخيه إلى إمامه فيبدأ بنفسه ثم بأخيه ثم بإمامه
يدخل فيه قولهم يسقي نخلة الثلث على وجه مخصوص في السقي

root_profile.summary: Bu kok etrafindaki dallar uc sayisi, ucte birlik pay, ucunculuk, uc parcali yapi ve bunlardan tureyen gun adi, deve-sagim, ocak kayasi, icecek, sikayet ve hurma sulama gibi dar ozel kullanimlara ayrilir.

contextual_glosses.text: üçte iki ve üçte birlik paylar

identity_judgment.rationale: Yetkili kaynak ifadesi dört sayısını, kırk sayısını, bir topluluğu dört kişiye çıkarma eylemini ve o topluluğun dördüncü üyesi olmayı birlikte doğrular. Geçici çerçeve bu sayısal çekirdeği ve sıra bildiren genişlemeyi doğru biçimde temsil eder.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın sayı biçimleri ile bir topluluğun dördüncü üyesi olmayı bildiren kalıp ayrı tutulur; kalıbın eylem anlamı sayı adlarının tümüne yayılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Dört sayısını ve bu sayının sıra bildiren kullanımını anlatır; ayrıca bir topluluğu dört kişiye çıkarma ya da topluluğun dördüncü üyesi olma eylemini kapsar.

facets.statement: Temel içerik dört sayısı ve onun sayı dizgesindeki biçimleridir.
Bir topluluğu dört kişiye çıkarma ve o toplulukta dördüncü olma, sayısal çekirdeğin eylemsel genişlemesidir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar dört ve kırk sayılarını, dörder dağıtım biçimini ve bir topluluğun dördüncüsü olma eylemini aynı sayısal eksende toplar. Hedef dilde adların dilbilgisel cinsiyetine göre ayrı dört biçimleri bulunmadığından iki kaynak biçimi aynı sözcükle karşılanır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Dört sayısı ile bir grubun dördüncü üyesi olma anlamının birlikte belirtilmesi gereken genel açıklamalarda kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Dört sayısını ve dördüncü sıraya katılma ilişkisini birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Salt sayı, sayma veya kırk gibi onluk bir sayı biçimi söz konusu olduğunda doğal karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Yalın sayısal çekirdeği eksiksiz korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir topluluğa katılarak onun dördüncü üyesi olmayı anlatan eylem bağlamlarında kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Topluluğun dördüncü üyesi olma ilişkisini korur.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal dört sayısını ve dördüncü olmayı anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal sekiz sayısını, sekizinci olmayı ve sekizde bir parçayı anlatır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da bir tam sayıyı ve o sayıya bağlı sıra ya da bölüm ilişkilerini işler.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Aynı sayı alanında bulunsalar da sayısal değerleri farklıdır; komşunun sekizde bir anlamı da odak dalın çekirdeğinde yoktur.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Verilen bütün sayı, bölüm, şiir ölçüsü ve kardeş dal adayları değerlendirildi. Sınırı en açık gösteren sekiz sayılı aday yayımlandı; ötekiler ya başka bir sayıyı yineledi ya da yalnız uzak bir çağrışım sundu.
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه عدد الأربعة والأربعون وصيرورة الشيء رابعا وصيغ رباع
branches.source_phrase_ar: ربعتهم أربعهم إذا كنت لهم رابعا (maqayis)؛ وربعت القوم فأنار رابعهم (ayn)؛ ربع القوم إذا صار رابعهم؛ أربعة ضرب من العدد (jamhara)؛ الأربعة في عدد المذكر والأربع في عدد المؤنث والأربعون بعد الثلاثين؛ أربع القوم أي صاروا أربعة (sihah)؛ ربعت القوم أربعهم إذا كنت لهم رابعا (tahdhib)؛ أربعة وأربعون وربع ورباع كلها من أصل واحد (mufradat)

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه الجزء الرابع من الشيء وأخذ ربع المال والمرباع الذي يأخذه الرئيس
يدخل فيه فتل الوتر أو الحبل أو العنان على أربع قوى وجعل الشيء مربعا
يدخل فيه ورد الإبل المسمى الربع وحمى الربع التي تعاود على هذه النوبة
يدخل فيه الربيع فصلا ومطرا وكلأ ونهرا ومنزل الربيع ورعي الإبل فيه ونتاج أول الربيع
يدخل فيه الإقامة بالمكان والدار والمحلة وأهل المنزل والوقوف والتمهل والأمر القديم المستقر
يدخل فيه رفع الحجر باليد ورفع الحمل بالمربعة والمشاركة في الحمل والقدرة على حمل الشيء
يدخل فيه وصف الإنسان أو الخيل باعتدال الخلق لا طويل ولا قصير أو مجتمع الخلق
يدخل فيه الرباعيات من الأسنان وسن الدابة إذا ألقت رباعيتها وصارت رباعا
يدخل فيه اسم اليوم الأربعاء وضبط بائه وجمعه
يدخل فيه هيئة القعود متربعا وما سمي الأربعاء أو الأربعاوى في القعود
يدخل فيه ارتباع البعير والربعة بمعنى أشد عدوه وضربه بقوائمه

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, havlayan hayvanı temel anlam olarak verir; dişil biçimi ve çoğul adları da aynı hayvan kavramının dil bilgisel uzantıları olarak gösterir. Bu çerçeve, av eğitimi, hastalık ve mecazi hırs anlamlarından açıkça ayrılır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Çıplak hayvan adı dalın çekirdeğidir; kurt ve su hayvanı için kullanılan birleşik adlar bu çekirdeğe genellenmez.

concept_map.definition: Havlamasıyla bilinen köpek türü hayvandır; dişisi ve farklı çoğul biçimleri aynı hayvan kavramına bağlıdır.

facets.statement: Havlayan ve genel olarak bilinen köpek türü hayvanı gösterir.
Hayvanın dişisini ve köpek topluluğunu bildiren biçimler aynı çekirdeğe bağlıdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, anlamı bilinen havlayan hayvan üzerinde birleştirir; dişi hayvanı ve çeşitli çoğul biçimleri de bu temel adın altında verir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Havlayan hayvanın genel ve yalın adı olarak dalın bütün çekirdek kapsamını karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: Hayvan türünün temel kimliğini ve genel adlandırmasını korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Söz konusu hayvanın özellikle dişi bireyi anlatıldığında doğal karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Köpek türünü ve dişi birey ayrımını korur.
error_profile.loses: Genel tür adını ve çoğul topluluk kapsamını dışarıda bırakır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal köpek denen hayvanın kendisini adlandırır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal köpek sahibi olan veya onu av için eğiten kişiyi adlandırır.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dalda köpek aynı av ve insan ilişkisi içinde yer alabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalın gönderimi hayvandır; komşunun gönderimi ise hayvan üzerinde sahiplik veya eğitim işlevi bulunan insandır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal sağlıklı ya da hastalığı belirtilmemiş hayvan türünün genel adıdır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal hastalığı, hastalanan canlıyı ve delilik benzeri belirtileri kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Hastalık köpekle ve köpek ısırığıyla ilişkilendirildiği için aynı sahnede buluşurlar.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Hayvanın tür adı hastalık anlamını içermez; hastalık dalı da köpek türünün genel adı değildir.

branches.neighbor_coverage_note: Bütün adaylar değerlendirildi; seçilen iki iç dal en güçlü okur karışıklıklarını gösterir, öteki hayvan adları ve uzak teknik dallar sınırı daha fazla keskinleştirmez.
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه الكلب والكلبة وجموعهما وما نُقل إليه من كلب البر وكلب الماء
branches.source_phrase_ar: الكلب وهو معروف والجمع كلاب وكليب (maqayis)؛ الكلب واحد الكلاب والأنثى بالهاء (ayn)؛ الكلب معروف ويجمع أكلبا وكلابا وكليبا (jamhara;sihah)؛ الكلب واحد الكلاب (tahdhib)؛ الكلب الحيوان النباح والأنثى كلبة (mufradat)

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه الكلاب والمكلب وصاحب الكلاب ومعلمها للصيد
يدخل فيه داء الكلب والكلب الكلب ومن عضه الكلب فكلب والعطاش والعواء والعض والجنون المشبه به
يدخل فيه اشتداد الحرص والتكالب على الشيء والمكالبة والمشارة والشر والأذى
يدخل فيه كلبة الزمان والشتاء والدهر وأرض كلبة ويبس النبات والشجرة العاردة الشوك
يدخل فيه السير أو القد الذي يجعل بين طرفي الأديم أو المزادة عند الخرز والكلبة والخرزة والخرز نفسه
يدخل فيه الحديدة العقفاء والكلاب والكلوب والمسمار في قائم السيف ومسمار الرحل والكلبتان وكلاليب البازي وما يمسك أو يعلق به
يدخل فيه ما سمي بالكلب أو الكلاب أو كليب من موضع أو جبل أو ماء أو نجم أو نبت أو قبيلة أو بطن

root_profile.summary: Kök; köpek hayvanından av köpeği eğiticisine, kuduzluk ve aşırı hırstan sert hava ile kuruluğa, deri dikişi tekniğine, kavrama araçlarına ve aktarılmış özel adlara uzanan çoklu bir anlam yapısı kurar. Bazı dallar benzetme ve işlev ilişkisiyle bağlanırken teknik araç ve özel ad dalları ayrı sözlüksel merkezler oluşturur.
